headline: Myers steadies Penn State in tight defensive grind over Miami
body: Penn State's offense found just enough rhythm to outlast Miami in a game where both defenses made their presence felt throughout. Mallik Myers completed 26 of 48 passes for 341 yards and a touchdown, proving efficient enough to navigate a Miami secondary that kept receivers from breaking free downfield. The real separation came on the ground, where Penn State's rushing attack — led by Jenkins and his one-yard touchdown plunge — generated 124 yards compared to Miami's anemic 54, a gap that proved decisive in a three-point finish.

Miami's passing game showed moments of competence through the work of receiver Jackson, who hauled in nine catches for 86 yards and provided a reliable safety valve for quarterback Mertz. Yet Mertz managed just 180 yards on 18 completions, a sign that Penn State's defensive front disrupted timing and rhythm in ways the box score alone doesn't capture. The Hurricanes' inability to establish anything resembling a ground game left them one-dimensional and predictable, a vulnerability Penn State's defense exploited without generating spectacular splash plays.

Neither team committed a turnover, which meant this came down to execution and field position. Penn State's 461 total yards versus Miami's 356 reflected a team that simply moved the ball with greater consistency. The three-point margin understates Penn State's control of this matchup — they dictated pace, leaned on the run, and made Myers a complementary piece rather than a franchise savior. Miami will rue opportunities left on the field, but the truth is Penn State's staff managed the game better when it mattered most.
turningPoint: Jenkins' touchdown run in the second half gave Penn State a two-score lead that Miami never recovered from, forcing the Hurricanes into a pass-first approach that negated their limited run game.

unsungHero.name: Taylor
unsungHero.why: Four catches for 80 yards kept chains moving and provided Myers with reliable targets on third downs, but his work went unheralded while Myers claimed all the spotlight despite an inconsistent completion percentage.
